- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3), model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a recent price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above prior peak.
- If sentiment turns negative mid-period, model delays downward correction; add 1–2 lagged days of downward bias.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30d moving avg, reduce by 2–5% unless sentiment is strong positive.
- For 30d horizon, model underestimates downward trends when sentiment is negative; add 1–3% downward bias for each negative sentiment day.
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, model overestimates short-term volatility; smooth forecast by reducing standard deviation by 15–20%.
